bib.title: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness", Haozhe Liu*, Tian Ye* et al. (NVIDIA, NTU, MIT; senior authors incl. Ping Luo, Enze Xie, Song Han). arXiv 2609.20519v1 [cs.AI], 17 Sep 2026 (page header dated 2026-08-17). Preprint, no venue.
COVERAGE: 15 of 15 pages, all text read (about 55k chars after removing a Figure 1 vector layer that repeats about 96k chars of label text on p.1). References skimmed. Figures were not rendered; I read only their extracted text and captions.

CORE CLAIM: An AI "auto-research loop" (an agent that reads traces, proposes harness changes and tests them) was run over 535 executable environments. It kept four token-saving mechanisms on top of the Pi coding harness. On the public EdgeBench set the full stack cuts tokens and cost about 44.7-49.0% and about a third, for a modest score loss. Search and held-out evaluation are kept strictly separate. The goal is cost, not capability.

HEADLINE NUMBERS (EdgeBench, 51 public tasks of 134; 11 used for one-way acceptance, 40 for final evaluation; costs at 17 Aug 2026 prices; no seeds, repeats or variance reported)
- GPT-5.6 Sol (the search backend), Pi vs SoL-Pi[Efficiency]: 2.1538B vs 1.0990B tokens, $1,339 vs $894, score 44.833 vs 42.003. That is 49.0% fewer tokens and about 93.7% of Pi's score. Codex: $1,787, score 34.738.
- Opus 5 (held-out backend, no re-search), Pi vs SoL-Pi: $1,741 vs $1,158, score 44.756 vs 42.224. Tokens fall 44.7% and cost 33.5%. Claude Code: $2,535, score 43.689.
- Single-mechanism add-ons to Pi: ObservationPack raises Sol score to 47.208 (+5.3%); Action Fusion raises Opus 5 to 50.482. Every mechanism lowers total tokens.
- Terminal-Bench 4 (63 CPU-only tasks): Codex and Pi solve 18, SoL-Pi solves 15. Cost is $211.12 vs Pi's $286.45. So it solves fewer tasks.
- IMO 2026 (6 problems, Lean 4, Sol xhigh): 3/6 passed for SoL-Pi and Pi, 5/6 for Codex. Cost per passed problem is $20.90 (SoL-Pi), $25.32 (Pi), $22.89 (Codex).
- Swarm, one 2-hour run each: SoL-Pi 1,127 cycles at $60.11; Pi swarm 1,366 cycles at $82.12; single agent 1,333 cycles at $39.20.

THE FOUR MECHANISMS (harness components)
- Action Fusion: edit plus follow-up command in one tool call.
- Online Context Compact: compact at plan-step boundaries when a cache-cost gate says it pays.
- ObservationPack: tool output over 10 KiB is archived to local storage and sent in full for 2 requests. After that the model sees a handle plus a head/tail excerpt, and can fetch exact pages.
- Evidence-Preserving Reducer: a cheaper model summarises build/test logs of 4 KiB or more, and a deterministic verifier checks the summary (schema, hash, exit code, quotes).
Relevant to the note: ObservationPack is the filesystem-as-memory primitive, and the verifier-with-fallback is a feedback-subsystem pattern.

QUOTES
- p.1: "reducing recorded token traffic by 44.7–49.0% and API cost by about one third"
- p.3: "Held-out results never feed back into the Auto-Research Loops: a failed validation rejects the candidate without triggering further optimization."
- p.3: "These counts describe the scope of our search; they do not establish a scaling law."
- p.9: "Despite the additional cache-write traffic, total model cost falls from $1,339 to $894."

HOW IT DIFFERS from your cited papers
- Target: efficiency (tokens and dollars), not task success.
- Method: it uses a large search over about 152 ideas and 535 environments, with a frozen held-out evaluation. This answers the overfitting worry in Wang et al. [20] (arXiv 2607.12227, 2026) that evolved harnesses overfit their search tasks, and it is a methodological contrast to Meta-Harness and Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE).
- Output: concrete, nameable mechanisms, not a score for a whole harness.
- It does not ablate the five subsystems. The add-one study (Table 4) is the only component ablation; there is no leave-one-out. I did not check what LIFE-Harness, Harness-R1 or JIT-Agent contain. The paper cites only Meta-Harness [17] and AHE [18] among your list.

LIMITS / NOT SHOWN
- Score drops about 6% at the full-stack point (42.0 vs 44.8). On Terminal-Bench 4 and IMO it solves fewer or equal problems, so "comparable performance" is generous.
- Single run per cell, no confidence intervals. n=51 tasks, with only 40 for final evaluation.
- Transfer is shown to one other model (Opus 5). The authors call the evidence "preliminary", and mechanisms trigger less often on Opus 5.
- Interaction effects are not isolated; the authors say their triggered-subset comparisons "do not isolate interaction effects".
- No scaling law. "Recursive efficient improvement" is stated as a vision, not shown.
- Results depend on Aug 2026 prices and prompt-cache pricing. The gate ignores the summarisation call's cost.
- All models are fictional-to-me frontier names (GPT-5.6 Sol, Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Luna). I took them from the text and could not verify them.
- The company authors are NVIDIA. Pi is a third-party toolkit (Earendil Works).

BUILDS ON
- Karpathy's autoresearch loop (GitHub, 2026).
- The Ralph Loop (Anthropic plugin, 2026).
- Meta-Harness (Lee et al., arXiv 2603.28052, 2026).
- AHE (Lin et al., arXiv 2604.25850, 2026).
- Recursive Harness Self-Improvement (Lee et al., arXiv 2607.15524, 2026).
- Darwin Gödel Machine (Zhang et al., ICLR 2026).
- Gödel Machine (Schmidhuber, 2007).
- ADAS (Hu et al., ICLR 2025).
- GEPA (ICLR 2026).
- SWE-agent (Yang et al., NeurIPS 2024).
- Reward-model overoptimization (Gao et al., ICML 2023), for the search/validation split.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Figure 4, p.5: "The four retained mechanisms act at different points in the agent-environment loop." It shows each mechanism's request path against the baseline, so it explains them faster than prose. Figure 2 on p.3 (separation of search and held-out evaluation) is the second choice.

VERDICT: Moderately on-topic. It is a solid, honest engineering paper on harness token efficiency, but only weakly about harness anatomy. Cite it for harness components that save tokens (output archival to disk, gated compaction, verified log reduction) and for held-out discipline in harness search. Do not cite it for the claim that a given subsystem matters for task success.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The page-1 extraction is polluted by repeated Figure 1 labels. Table 1/2 cell alignment is slightly ambiguous in places (cache-read vs write columns), but the cost and score numbers above are consistent across Tables 1, 2 and 4.
